_what_this_is: One ceiling per governance container. A CEILING IS THE FOURTH KIND OF COUNT IN THIS REPOSITORY and is NOT a ratchet: a ratchet tracks a defect count that ought to reach zero, a ceiling tracks a structural size that must not. Read by the surface budget step in .github/workflows/backend-checks.yml, which fails rather than defaulting when this file is missing, empty or unparseable, and which asserts set equality between these keys and the metrics it measures IN BOTH DIRECTIONS -- a container with no budget is ungoverned, and a budget with no container is a number that looks authoritative and governs nothing.
_how_the_numbers_were_set: By replaying 754 first-parent commits (2026-05-30 to 2026-08-31) and measuring every container at each one. Every increase was classified as one that should or should not have been blocked, and each ceiling sits at or above the largest legitimate one, with the commit that set it named in its why field. NO NUMBER HERE CAME FROM A JUDGEMENT ABOUT WHAT LOOKED RIGHT. Two kinds came out of that. Where a standing rule makes growth RECUR -- the rule that a batch corrects what it makes false adds lines to CLAUDE.md without adding a rule -- the ceiling carries headroom the size of the largest legitimate single commit. Where growth is a discrete deliberate act, the ceiling is pinned, and the why field says the replay supports the pin rather than merely that a pin looked prudent.
_what_a_ceiling_cannot_see: A CEILING FIRES UPWARD ONLY, SO EMPTYING A CONTAINER IS INVISIBLE TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION, AND THAT IS TRUE OF ALL 24. Nothing here notices a rule deleted from CLAUDE.md, a deny rule or a hook removed from .claude/settings.json, a skill or a workflow step deleted, or a correct-work case dropped -- every one of those makes a number go DOWN and every one passes. Floors are a different check and live elsewhere: MIN_RULES_FILES=1 in the step above this one is the only floor under any of these 24 containers, and the other 23 have none. THE ONE SHRINK THAT IS REFUSED is .claude/settings.json going missing altogether, because the step reads that file and refuses a missing input rather than defaulting to an empty one; the same file kept in place with every list emptied still passes, and cw-12b stores exactly that so the gap is visible in something that runs. This paragraph is not a check and does not pretend to be one. It says which half of the range these numbers cover, for the same reason not_gated below names what is outside the tree instead of omitting it and looking complete.
_raising_one: Raising a ceiling is normal and expected. Do it in the SAME COMMIT as the growth and rewrite the why field to name what set the new number. The container this file exists for refilled one defensible paragraph at a time, and every one of those paragraphs would have been approved on its own; what was missing was a place where the total was visible.
_measured_at: 2026-08-31, branch ci/surface-budget, by the step that reads this file, RE-MEASURED after the eight fixes from plexive-docs/research/surface-budget-verification-2026-08-31.md, and correct_work_cases RE-MEASURED AGAIN at 29 on branch fix/skills-loading, where its ceiling was also re-set to 39, and AGAIN at 31 on branch fix/hook-stdin-utf8 (2026-09-02, cw-17a-b), where its ceiling was re-set to 41 in the same commit as the growth. claude_md_bytes, claude_md_lines and claude_md_unconditional_rules were RE-MEASURED AGAIN on 2026-09-02 on branch docs/claude-md-reason-move, which shrank CLAUDE.md from 27741 to 26478 index bytes and added the paragraph closing it to additions; claude_md_bytes' ceiling was re-set in the same commit and claude_md_unconditional_rules reached its ceiling of 8. Every other number below still dates from the ci/surface-budget run. Three numbers moved for a reason other than growth and each is a CORRECTED MEASUREMENT rather than a container shrinking: claude_md_unconditional_rules stayed 7 but stopped counting continuation lines, workflow_named_thresholds went 18 -> 12 because it now counts distinct names rather than assignments and because MIN_BUDGET_ENTRIES was removed, and every container measured from a directory now counts what git ls-files reports rather than what this filesystem holds. architecture_md_bytes WAS ADDED 2026-09-03 on branch docs/architecture-trim-batch-4, the twenty-fourth container, measured at 243187 LF bytes in the same commit that set its ceiling; the step gained the matching metric in that commit too, because set equality is asserted in both directions and a budget with no metric is refused as loudly as a metric with no budget.

claude_md_bytes.why: SET BY f2f49f95 (2026-08-31, +2809 bytes) AND CARRIED FORWARD AT THAT WIDTH: the ceiling is the measured size plus 2809, re-set whenever the measured size moves, so exactly one correction of that shape always fits and the one after it must come here. The increase that set the width is the largest the replay classifies as one that should not have been blocked: it recorded the exact commands the three required checks run, which the same-batch documentation rule required. Headroom is exactly that commit's size, so the next correction of that shape passes and the one after it must raise this number. Every larger increase in the replay is from the 2026-08-27..29 run that took CLAUDE.md to 135770 bytes, and the shrink at ed645fcf removed 93987 of them, which is the project's own verdict on those. THIS IS A BACKSTOP AGAINST SILENT DOUBLING, NOT A FENCE: it does not stop a drip of defensible paragraphs, which is exactly how the container refilled. The fence is claude_md_sections, claude_md_rules and claude_md_unconditional_rules, which prose cannot move. RE-SET 2026-09-02 AGAINST A SMALLER FILE, 30464 -> 29287, in the same commit as the shrink: reasoning carried in full in docs/RULE_HISTORY.md, docs/CI_NOTES.md, backend/app/auth.py and tools/surface-budget.json was removed from CLAUDE.md, and the paragraph closing the file to additions was added. THE +2809 WIDTH IS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED. Pinning this to the measured size would red cw-8-claude-md-correction-within-ceiling, which appends a 36-line correction and declares EXPECT_RC=0, and would falsify docs/CI_NOTES.md:203, which records this width.

claude_md_lines.why: SET BY f2f49f95 (2026-08-31, +36 lines), the same commit and the same reasoning as claude_md_bytes. Seven of the twelve post-shrink commits to CLAUDE.md changed ZERO lines, because a correction rewords a paragraph in place, so this number moves only when a paragraph is added. cw-8 stores a 36-line correction sitting exactly on this ceiling; tightening this to a pin turns that case red, which is why it is stored. RE-SET 179 -> 189 ON 2026-09-02, measured 143 -> 153: the paragraph closing this file to additions is ten lines, and the width stays exactly cw-8's 36 because that is what this number means. THE RAISE WAS FOUND BY RUNNING cw-8, NOT BY ARITHMETIC. The batch that added those ten lines shrank CLAUDE.md by 1263 bytes and left this ceiling alone, so cw-8 -- correct work, EXPECT_RC=0 -- red at 189 against 179 while every gate on the branch was green. A shrink can still push a stored correct-work input over a ceiling, because the ceiling is measured plus a fixed width and the width moves with the measurement.

claude_md_sections.why: WHAT IT COUNTS, IN THE WORDS A PERSON WOULD USE: lines beginning "## " that are OUTSIDE fenced code blocks. A heading quoted inside a fence is a quotation, not a section, and counting one took this to 11 against the pin on 2026-08-31 (stored as cw-14). PINNED, AND THE REPLAY SUPPORTS THE PIN. Only two commits ever took this above 10: 4c585a79 (9->11) and 066c4b38 (11->14), and the shrink removed exactly those sections again. Every section standing today was added at or below 10, so this pin would have blocked nothing that should not have been blocked. A new '## ' heading is a deliberate act, and the pin costs one line in this file in the same commit, where a reader sees the decision.

claude_md_rules.why: WHAT IT COUNTS, IN THE WORDS A PERSON WOULD USE: the top-level "- " bullets at column 0 under "## Rules". A line indented under a bullet is part of that bullet, not a rule of its own. SET BY b98b8209 (2026-08-28, 6->7), which added the execution-discipline bullet that is still in CLAUDE.md today, so a pin at the measured 6 would have blocked work that stood. Margin is one rule. The count returned to 6 only because 38d3ef68 moved the emoji rule out to .claude/rules/, which is the question reaching 7 again should trigger rather than a number to raise quietly. THE ANSWER TO THIS CONTAINER REDDING IS NOT TO RAISE THIS NUMBER, since 2026-09-02 and the paragraph closing CLAUDE.md to additions: it is to name the register entry that authorised the addition, or to take the addition out. The step's own closing advice is generic across all 24 containers and says the opposite, so it is wrong for this container and for claude_md_unconditional_rules.

claude_md_unconditional_rules.why: WHAT IT COUNTS, IN THE WORDS A PERSON WOULD USE: RULES, WHERE A RULE IS AN OPENING LINE. Under "## Rules", a top-level "- " bullet at column 0 opens a rule, and so does the first line of a blank-line-separated paragraph at column 0. Continuation lines of a wrapped bullet or paragraph, and sub-bullets indented under a rule, belong to the rule above them. Six bullets and one paragraph is 7. REFORMATTING MUST NOT MOVE THIS NUMBER, and until 2026-08-31 it did: the metric was bullets plus paragraph-runs, so wrapping two bullets at 98 columns read 9 and wrapping all six read 11, with no rule added and no text changed. cw-9a..cw-9d store those inputs. THE ONE SHAPE STILL COUNTED WRONG is a continuation line that itself begins "- ", which no parser can tell from a bullet; cw-9e pins it, no bullet here contains a standalone hyphen token, and it is left alone deliberately. THE CEILING WAS SET BY 42df1f56 (2026-08-29, 7->8), the shrink merge, which added the rule that a step watching for a condition reports its own failure -- the central rule of this repository, and still present. A pin at the measured 7 would have blocked it. Margin is one rule. MEASURED 8 SINCE 2026-09-02, WHICH IS THE CEILING: the paragraph closing this file to additions is itself an opening line under "## Rules", so it counts as one. The margin is now zero, and that is the intended state rather than an oversight -- the container is full because the file is closed, and the next addition must be defended here before it can land. THE ANSWER TO THIS CONTAINER REDDING IS NOT TO RAISE THIS NUMBER: it is to name the register entry that authorised the addition, or to take the addition out.

claude_rules_files.why: THE SLOT IS SPENT AND THE CEILING DID NOT MOVE, 2026-09-03 on branch docs/architecture-entry-standard: .claude/rules/architecture-md.md is the second file and it lands UNDER the existing ceiling, so this row records growth without authorising any. Margin is now zero, which is the mechanism working rather than a state to fix -- a third rules file must be defended here before it can land, and the step was run against one to see it refused (claude_rules_files 3 / 2, OVER, exit 1). SET BY tools/correct-work/cases/cw-7-second-scoped-rules-file.sh, not by a commit. That case exists to prove a SECOND correctly scoped rules file is correct work, so a pin at the measured 1 would red on a stored correct-work input, which is the inverse defect CLAUDE.md keeps apart from the rest. The floor under this same container is MIN_RULES_FILES=1 in the step above it, so the container is fenced at both ends by two different assertions on purpose.

workflow_named_thresholds.why: WHAT IT COUNTS, IN THE WORDS A PERSON WOULD USE: distinct MIN_*, MAX_* and *_PIN threshold NAMES, per workflow file. The same name written twice in one file -- an assignment and the env-prefixed use that carries it into a heredoc, which is the idiom these files use -- is one threshold. The same name in two files is two. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-31 AND THE NUMBER CAME DOWN: the metric counted assignments BY SHAPE until then, so backend-checks.yml's ten matching lines were seven thresholds, and the 18 that was measured was 13. The old why field claimed a +2 for the batch that added this file; that never happened, the batch added ONE threshold and the shape regex counted it twice. Replaying the by-name count over the first-parent history gives three changes: 0 -> 11 at 7d2a0c0c, the merge that created every gate assertion at once, then +1 at 8261e3a (MIN_RULES_FILES) and +1 at 06d1803 (MIN_BUDGET_ENTRIES). The largest legitimate single-commit increase that is not the creation is therefore ONE, and the ceiling is measured + 1. MEASURED 12 RATHER THAN 13 because MIN_BUDGET_ENTRIES was removed in the commit before this one for being unable to fire. Two new thresholds in one commit now cost a line here, and that line is honest: it records thresholds that exist. cw-15a, cw-15b and cw-15c store all three directions. The four bare-literal thresholds in backend-checks.yml are NOT counted and are named in docs/CI_NOTES.md instead, so this number is a floor under the naming convention as much as a ceiling over the count.

correct_work_cases.why: 42 = 32 + 10, RE-SET 2026-09-02 on branch feat/stop-hook-rule-log with cw-18, the allow direction for the Stop hook's refusal detector: a transcript of ordinary failures for which it must record nothing. IT IS RE-SET HERE BECAUSE THE COUNT MOVED, which is the rule this field states about itself and which it has already been caught not following once. THE WIDTH, +10, WAS SET BY 7d2a0c0c (2026-08-31, +10 cases) and is carried forward: the ceiling is the measured count plus 10, re-set when the count moves. 41 = 31 + 10, re-set 2026-09-02 on fix/hook-stdin-utf8 with cw-17a-b, the pair that pins check_emoji against a payload carrying the emoji as raw UTF-8 bytes; it was 39 = 29 + 10, re-set 2026-08-31 on fix/skills-loading. IT WAS NOT RE-SET IN THE COMMIT THAT MOVED THE COUNT, which is the thing _raising_one asks for: 7dd9170 took the count 27 -> 29 and left the ceiling at 37, a width of 8, so the field declared a rule it had just stopped following and no reader could tell whether 37 was deliberate. Nothing failed -- 29 is under 37 either way -- and that is what made it invisible. Measured 12 until 2026-08-31, then 27 when the fifteen inputs from the surface-budget verification landed at once, then 29 the same day with cw-16a-b, the first pair here that exercises a HOOK rather than a CI step -- itself an increase of 15, larger than the 10 this width was derived from. THIS CEILING GOVERNS ALMOST NOTHING AND THAT IS SAID RATHER THAN HIDDEN: 10 of headroom on a container of 29 stops a generator dumping cases and stops nothing else. It is kept because growth here is the one kind that is unambiguously good -- every case is evidence that a gate does not red on correct work -- and because a container that is measured is one somebody can see move.

architecture_md_bytes.why: THE UNIT IS LF BYTES, WHICH IS THE RUNNER'S UNIT AND NOT THIS MACHINE'S. The step reads the file through read_lf(), the checkout on the runner is LF, and the working tree on the Windows machine these files are written on is CRLF and reads larger by exactly its carriage-return count -- 243671 against 243198 on 2026-09-03, a difference of 473, which is the line count. THAT PAIR WAS 243659 / 243187 UNTIL THIS COMMIT AND BOTH HALVES WERE STALE BY 7: 028d176 and 4bf51e1 changed ARCHITECTURE.md after the ceiling was set on the same branch and left this field alone, so the recorded measurement described a blob that never reached main. Nothing failed, because the step compares the BUDGET and reads 'measured' as documentation -- which is exactly how it drifted. A budget set against one and checked against the other would be wrong by that much, which is the same reason claude_md_bytes is measured this way. SET 2026-09-03 ON BRANCH docs/architecture-trim-batch-4, in the same commit as the measurement, at the state the fourth and last trim batch leaves behind. 254744 = 243187 + 11557. THE WIDTH CAME FROM A REPLAY AND NOT FROM A JUDGEMENT: every first-parent commit that changed ARCHITECTURE.md was measured (311 of them, 300 increases, median +426), and the largest increase that is ordinary batch growth is +11557 at f0b957d7 (2026-08-30), the settings-enforcement merge, whose additions are still in the file today. The one larger increase, +67486 at 615c8fc4, is a 46-commit upstream sync of a long-lived integration branch and is not growth of this container in the sense a ceiling is about. Every merge here is the unit of change, because a commit cannot reach main any other way, so the width is merge-sized on purpose. WHY HEADROOM AND NOT A PIN: CLAUDE.md requires that ARCHITECTURE.md be updated after every change, one entry per new or changed item, so growth RECURS by standing rule exactly as it does for CLAUDE.md, and a pin at the measured size would red on the next ordinary batch. THIS IS A BACKSTOP AGAINST SILENT DOUBLING AND NOT A FENCE. It does not stop a drip of defensible entries, which is how this file reached 284447 LF bytes by 2026-09-02 (36a927a, the state the four trim batches started from; the 284952 this field carried until 2026-09-03 was that same blob read CRLF) before four trim batches took it to 243187; nothing measured the total while that happened, and this row is what would have made it visible. It also fires UPWARD ONLY, so the file emptying is invisible to it, which is true of all 24 and is what _what_a_ceiling_cannot_see is about.
